types.name: BankAccountFilter
types.description:
An account: its identity, and the history of every syncer and import that fed it.

What reaches the account at a provider lives on its :class:`AccountSyncer` rows (one per
provider identity); an account with no syncer is fed only by imports (a bank that is no

One consent at one bank (an Enable Banking session) or one Scalable Capital login.

A Scalable connection keeps its credentials — the DPoP private key and the rotating refresh
token bound to it — Fernet-encrypted in ``secret`` (see :mod:`finance.scalable.crypto`).

Also every GraphQL error's `extensions.code`.

types.name: CategoryFilter
types.description:
A spending or income category. Categories nest (groceries under food).

A category's ``kind`` is always its root's: the whole subtree is expense, income or
transfer, so stats and budgets never disagree about a child. Base categories carry the
``key`` of their node in :mod:`finance.taxonomy`; everything about them stays editable.
Name + description are embedded, which is what lets a never-seen merchant land in the
right category (:mod:`finance.semantic`).

fields.description: The bank's own reference, when it sends one.

fields.name: isTransfer
fields.description: Money moved between own accounts; excluded from stats.

fields.name: isTransferManual
fields.description: ``is_transfer`` was set by a user and is not recomputed.

fields.name: isin
fields.description: The security traded or paying out, if any.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: The provider's transaction type (Scalable: BUY, SELL, DEPOSIT, DISTRIBUTION, INTEREST, FEE, TAX, …); null for bank transactions.

fields.name: merchant
fields.description: Who the transaction was with.

fields.name: merchantLocation
fields.description: Where: the merchant's store, when the line names one.

fields.name: merchantSource
fields.description: How the merchant was set (AUTO by alias, MANUAL by a user).

fields.name: note
fields.description: A user's note.

fields.name: origin
fields.description: Whether the bank fields were synced or imported from a file.

fields.name: quantity
fields.description: Units of the security, if any.

fields.name: remittance
fields.description: The remittance information (purpose line).

fields.name: semanticInput
fields.description: The exact text this transaction is embedded as: its bank line (normalized: no numbers, 'DANKT', cities or legal forms), then what its merchant and place add. Two lines are similar when these texts are.

fields.name: similarTransactions
fields.description: The organization's transactions most similar to this one (same merchant, same kind of payment), closest first. `maxDistance` (cosine, 0–2) drops the far ones.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Booked or pending.

fields.name: suggestedCategories
fields.description: The categories this transaction most likely belongs to, best first — from similar transactions the organization categorized and from category terms. Empty when it has no embedding yet.

fields.name: syncer
fields.description: The syncer that last wrote the bank fields; null for imported rows.

fields.name: transactionDate
fields.description: When it was made (e.g. the card payment).

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: When the row last changed.

fields.name: valueDate
fields.description: When it took effect for interest.

types.name: TransactionFilter
types.description:
A single booked or pending transaction on an account.

Counterparty, remittance and provider kind are embedded: similar transactions (the same
merchant, the same kind of payment) sit close together, which drives ``search``,
``similarTransactions`` and category suggestions (:mod:`finance.semantic`).

Bank fields are overwritten by every sync; ``category``, ``note`` and ``is_transfer``
belong to the users and survive re-syncs of booked rows (see :mod:`finance.sync`).

A row is SYNC (a syncer wrote it) or IMPORT (a statement import did). A sync that finds the
same booking as an IMPORT row takes that row over instead of adding a second one
(:mod:`finance.matching`), keeping its category, note and ``import_raw``.

inputFields.name: near
inputFields.description: Only transactions at a merchant location within `radiusMeters` of a point, nearest first.

inputFields.name: nearCategory
inputFields.description: Keep transactions that look like they belong to this category — close to what the organization put there, or to one of its terms — closest first.

inputFields.name: search
inputFields.description: Search by text: a case-insensitive substring of counterparty, remittance or note; semantic similarity to them; or a category whose terms mean the text ("supermarket" finds what is in Groceries). Substring matches rank first, then by similarity; an explicit `ordering` replaces that ranking.

inputFields.name: similarTo
inputFields.description: Order by similarity to the given transaction, nearest first (no cut-off, composes with other filters and pagination). Empty when it is not in this organization or has no embedding yet.

types.name: TransactionKind
types.description: A provider's transaction type (Scalable's broker and savings types). OTHER is a type this service does not know yet.

types.name: TransactionOrigin
types.description: Where a transaction's bank fields came from: a syncer (SYNC), or a file import (IMPORT) — a sync that finds the same booking later takes an IMPORT row over, keeping its category and note.

types.name: TransactionStatus
types.description: Booking status as reported by the bank.

types.name: UnmappedImportCategory
types.description: An imported category pair no category is mapped to (yet): its rows stay uncategorized, for rules and suggestions.

types.name: UpdateBudgetInput
types.description: Changes to a budget; omitted fields stay as they are.

types.name: UpdateCategoryInput
types.description: Changes to a category; omitted fields stay as they are.

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description: Only for a top-level category; the whole subtree follows.

inputFields.name: parent
inputFields.description: The new parent, or null to make it top-level. Moving takes the new root's kind.

types.name: UpdateCategoryRuleInput
types.description: Changes to a rule; omitted fields stay as they are.

types.name: UpdateMerchantInput
types.description: Changes to a merchant; omitted fields stay as they are.

inputFields.name: category
inputFields.description: The default category, or null for none; its transactions follow.

inputFields.name: categoryKey
inputFields.description: …or the default category by its base key.

inputFields.name: key
inputFields.description: A new key — only when you mean to change what clients link by.

inputFields.name: name
inputFields.description: A new display name; the `key` stays (links by key keep working).

types.name: UpdateMerchantLocationInput
types.description: Changes to a place; omitted fields stay as they are.

types.name: UpdateMerchantRuleInput
types.description: Changes to a merchant rule; omitted fields stay as they are.

inputFields.name: location
inputFields.description: A place to pin, or null to let the store number decide.

types.name: UpsertMerchantInput
types.description: Create a merchant, or update the one with this key. Omitted fields keep their value on update; `aliases` are added (never removed).

inputFields.name: aliases
inputFields.description: Texts to add as aliases (the key itself is always one).

inputFields.name: key
inputFields.description: What the merchant is found by; normalized ("McDonald's" → "mcdonald").

inputFields.name: name
inputFields.description: Display name; the key's text when creating without one.

types.name: User
types.description: A user account; sub is the stable subject identifier from the identity provider.

types.name: ValuationPoint
types.description: The depot on one day: its value, what was put in, and the gain.

fields.name: invested
fields.description: Net money put into securities up to this day (buys and savings plans minus sells).

types.name: VisitStats
types.description: When and how often: visits are distinct days with a transaction.

fields.name: visitsPerMonth
fields.description: Visits per 30.44 days of the window.

types.name: WeekdayTotals
types.description: Totals for one ISO weekday (1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday).

types.name: WindowInfo
types.description: The window a view covered, and the one it was compared with.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description: A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a __DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

enumValues.name: QUERY
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a query operation.

enumValues.name: MUTATION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a mutation operation.

enumValues.name: SUBSCRIPTION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a subscription operation.

enumValues.name: FIELD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment definition.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_SPREAD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment spread.

enumValues.name: INLINE_FRAGMENT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an inline fragment.

enumValues.name: VARIABLE_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a variable definition.

enumValues.name: SCHEMA
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a schema definition.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a scalar definition.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an object type definition.

enumValues.name: FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field definition.

enumValues.name: ARGUMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an argument definition.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an interface definition.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a union definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM_VALUE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum value definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object type definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object field definition.

enumValues.name: DIRECTIVE_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a directive definition.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description: One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Field
types.description: Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description: Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and optionally a default value.

fields.name: defaultValue
fields.description: A GraphQL-formatted string representing the default value for this input value.

types.name: __Schema
types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

directives.name: deprecated
directives.description: Marks an element of a GraphQL schema as no longer supported.

args.name: reason
args.description: Explains why this element was deprecated, usually also including a suggestion for how to access supported similar data. Formatted using the Markdown syntax, as specified by [CommonMark](https://commonmark.org/).

directives.name: include
directives.description: Directs the executor to include this field or fragment only when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: skip
directives.description: Directs the executor to skip this field or fragment when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: specifiedBy
directives.description: Exposes a URL that specifies the behavior of this scalar.

args.name: url
args.description: The URL that specifies the behavior of this scalar.
